submitted.rationale: Index 18 (Sb 0.674, near stoichiometric CoSb2O6) had the highest measured EQE: 8.4e-4 %. MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom). All EQE values on this line are very small, so the whole library responds weakly at 2.4 eV.

rejected.reason: Co7Sb2O12 spinel region; measured EQE was negative (-6.5e-3 %)
Sb-rich end; measured EQE 7.1e-4 %, slightly below index 18. MEGNet puts the Sb2O3 gap at 3.77 eV, above the 2.4 eV photon energy

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 (Sb 0.667) on the hull (0 eV/atom). That makes a phase-pure, stable oxide likely at index 18 (Sb 0.674). MEGNet's HSE gap of 0.37 eV is implausibly low for a Co2+ antimonate, which is known experimentally to absorb in the visible at around 2 eV or more. I treat the gap as unreliable and do not count it against this candidate.

Moderate support. MACE puts Co7Sb2O12 spinel (Sb 0.222) close to the hull at 0.03 eV/atom, so it is likely to form near index 5 (Sb 0.235). MEGNet's HSE gap of 1.44 eV is below the 2.4 eV photon energy, so it would absorb. The trirutile side gave near-zero EQE, which makes the Co-rich spinel region the next region to test.

Mixed. MEGNet gives Sb2O3 a 3.77 eV gap, which is too wide to absorb 2.4 eV photons on its own. At the Sb-rich end, though, the film would be a mixture of Sb oxide and CoSb2O6 with dilute Co that may add sub-gap absorption. This is the least-explored end of the composition line and is the GP's top UCB pick. The two measured regions gave near-zero EQE, so this final measurement goes to exploring the unmeasured end.
